issue_context.title: Revisit PatternContext<TFrame>.PushDataFrame nullable annotation
issue_context.body:
### Description

See the conversation here: https://github.com/dotnet/core/pull/7211#discussion_r810075469

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/57398 annotated `PushDataFrame` as allowing a nullable `TFrame` argument. However, it doesn't make sense to push a `null` frame, and would lead to other issues if we did.

Note that the `TFrame` is currently only ever used with a `struct` type, which can never be `null`.

### Reproduction Steps

Call `PatternContext<TFrame>.PushDataFrame` with a `null`.

### Expected behavior

It should give a "this parameter should not be `null`" warning.

### Actual behavior

It allows `null` values without a warning.

### Regression?

No.

### Known Workarounds

_No response_

### Configuration

_No response_

### Other information

_No response_

review_comments: Couldn't we just leave this as `protected TFrame? Frame;` and just change `protected void PushDataFrame(TFrame? frame)` => `protected void PushDataFrame(TFrame frame)`?
We could. But `null` could still be pushed in `_stack` in that case, is that ok? Or it's out of scope of this issue and we should just fix annotations here?

I think it depends on whether the breaking change is acceptable or not. If we can accept the breaking change, we won't have to worry about this. But if we can't take the breaking change, I think this approach is the next best thing.

> But null could still be pushed in _stack in that case, is that ok?

It wouldn't affect the rest of the public API, right? the stack is private.

> It wouldn't affect the rest of the public API, right? the stack is private.

Yes, stack's nullability info is private, but `Frame`s isn't, and if consumers don't really check `Frame` for null in case of non-empty stack like @stephentoub told, that (`Frame = _stack.Pop();`) may be an issue.

> But if we can't take the breaking change, I think this approach is the next best thing.

Yeah, if breaking changes are not acceptable, `PushDataFrame(TFrame frame)` and `where TFrame : notnull` would do the trick

I believe this is a breaking change. The type is in an `Internal` namespace and I'm not sure others actually use this.

cc @terrajobst @adamsitnik @Jozkee - thoughts on whether this break is "worth it"?

Welp, people is not supposed to use this type. As per the [docs](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.extensions.filesystemglobbing.internal.patterncontexts.patterncontext-1.pushdataframe?view=dotnet-plat-ext-6.0):
> This API supports infrastructure and is not intended to be used directly from your code. This API may change or be removed in future releases.

IMO is not worth correcting (file a breaking change doc for something that no one is supposed to use) "internal" APIs like this one.

> (file a breaking change doc for something that no one is supposed to use)

OTOH, If this is not an inconvenient at all, we can do whatever we want to this API.
Well the docs say "This API may change". So I'm OK with changing it. Are the area-owners OK with it?  @dotnet/area-extensions-filesystem ?
I'm one owner and I'm OK with it :)
